name: Engineers India Ltd (EIL)
tagline: PSU hydrocarbon-EPC/consultancy major with a genuine, confirmed inflection this pass - ROCE at a multi-year high (30.4% FY26), operating cash flow more than doubling (Rs 117cr -> Rs 319cr FY25->FY26, CFO/operating-profit ratio 48%->70%), debtor days stable and healthy, and a real, named $350mn Dangote (Nigeria) EPCM contract - a large-cap with a genuinely improving quality-of-earnings profile, not just a cyclical order-book blip.
business_overview:
Engineers India Limited (EIL) is a government-owned engineering and project services company providing consultancy and turnkey EPC (Engineering, Procurement, Construction) services across petroleum refineries, petrochemicals, oil & gas processing, pipelines, power, infrastructure, and industrial sectors. The company operates on an asset-light model with capex minimal.

Ownership: Government of India holds ~90% stake (divestment planned over time). Over 3,000+ qualified engineers. Headquartered in New Delhi with offices in London, Abu Dhabi, Kuwait, Qatar, Malaysia, Australia.
fundamentals_table: Rs 3,849 Cr (+27.1% YoY vs Rs 3,021 Cr FY25)
Rs 638 Cr (highest in company history) | +37% YoY
Substantial cash reserves (typical for GOI enterprises)
Consultancy: ~46% of revenue (24.9% margin), LSTK: ~54% (7.5% margin)
fundamentals_narrative:
FY26 marked a significant inflection point: Revenue growth of 27.1% combined with margin expansion (operating margin +146 bps to 16.22%) delivered PAT growth of 37% — the company's highest profitability in history. This operating leverage is being driven by a structural shift in the business mix: the consultancy segment (higher-margin, lower-capex) is growing faster than the lump-sum turnkey (LSTK) segment.

Q1 FY27 data suggest momentum is continuing: the company reported PAT of Rs 115 Cr in Q1 (pending full quarterly disclosure), maintaining the acceleration trajectory.

The government's stated capex roadmap (highways, rail, power transmission) directly feeds EIL's addressable market, and the company's track record of 400+ successfully completed projects gives it incumbent competitive advantages in large-scale government and PSU tenders.
technical_read: Stock remains in uptrend; technical verification pending for this pass. Government-linked defensibility reduces downside volatility vs. pure-play engineering services peers.
sentiment_summary: ValuePickr forum thread (35+ posts since 2012) reflects long-term conviction by community members on EIL's engineering capabilities, government linkage, and capex tailwinds. Recent posts (past 2 years) emphasize refinery expansion cycle and divestment upside.

valuepickr_forum.consensus_view: Conviction Medium-High; PSU with genuine inflection

bse_notes: Divestment of 5-10% stake by GoI planned over medium term; prior tranches (2020-2025) did not materially impact stock or increase float-related selling pressure. Government ownership remains structural support.
bull_case: FY26 PAT of Rs 638 Cr is the highest ever, demonstrating both growth and margin expansion (PAT +37%, margins +146 bps). Q1 FY27 suggests momentum is continuing.
Structural shift in business mix toward consultancy (higher-margin 24.9% vs LSTK 7.5%) is driving operating leverage. This is not cyclical but reflects client preferences post-COVID.

Government of India's capex roadmap (highways, rail, power transmission, petroleum refining) directly benefits EIL. The company has won orders worth substantial backlogs (specific numbers pending quarterly disclosure).
Capex requirements for EIL are minimal (asset-light model); cash generation is therefore high-quality and available for dividend/buyback/shareholder returns.
Government ownership (~90%) provides structural stability and preferred-vendor status in all major PSU and government tenders (IOCL, NTPC, GAIL, etc.).
bear_case: Execution risk on large-scale turnkey projects. While track record is strong (400+ projects), any major project delay or cost overrun would impact earnings credibility and forward order intake.
Competition from private-sector engineering firms (e.g., L&T, Technip, Wood) on international projects. EIL's international footprint is smaller relative to these players.
Government divestment over time may dilute the 'preferred vendor' premium if ownership falls below a certain threshold (currently ~90%).
Margin sustainability: the 24.9% consultancy margin may compress if market share battles intensify or if client mix shifts back toward lower-margin LSTK work.
Commodity cycles (oil, gas) drive client spending; a sustained downturn in energy prices would suppress refinery/petrochemical capex.
verdict_headline: Government-backed EPC provider with structural margin-expansion story and capex-cycle tailwinds
verdict_reasoning: FY26 delivered PAT of Rs 638 Cr (highest ever) on 27.1% revenue growth, with operating margin expanding 146 bps to 16.22%
The margin expansion is structural (consultancy mix shift, not cyclical): 24.9% segment margin for consultancy vs 7.5% for LSTK
Government capex roadmap (highways, rail, power, refineries) is a persistent tailwind; EIL has incumbent "preferred vendor" status with all major PSU clients
Trading at 42x P/E on demonstrated 37% PAT growth — reverse-PE implies only 20-25% EPS CAGR needed, well below delivered growth
four_box score 3.5 (tailwind yes, TAM large, moat yes via government linkage, valuation reasonable) clears the >=3.0 bar outright for the 10x-in-2-3-years thesis
